text: Jennings (1906) described a graded avoidance sequence in the sessile ciliate Stentor coeruleus. Which ordering reflects his escalating hierarchy from least to most disruptive?
choices: Detachment and swimming away first, then contraction, then bending
Contraction first, then bending, with detachment never occurring
Bending away, then reversing the oral cilia, then contraction, then detachment and swimming away
Immediate detachment on first contact, with no intermediate responses
explanation: Jennings reported escalation from the cheapest to the most disruptive response: bend away, reverse the oral cilia, contract (repeatedly), and finally detach and swim off, escalating only when the irritant persists. The reversed order (choice 0), a truncated sequence lacking detachment (choice 1), and immediate detachment (choice 3) all misrepresent the try-cheapest-first logic of the hierarchy.
